prompt:
Create a production game-animation sprite sheet of the little cream and vermilion three-tailed fox in the first reference, matching its chunky early-PS1 low-poly design, angular geometry, small blue-gray pixel eyes, charcoal paws and pixelated diffuse textures. The other references, when supplied, are the exact connection poses or same-character examples.
Exactly 12 full-body poses arranged in a regular 3 columns by 4 rows grid, chronological reading order. Orthographic three-quarter view facing right, identical camera, scale, lighting, anatomy, markings and proportions throughout. Exactly four limbs (two forelegs, two hindlegs), exactly three tails. Raised forepaws are the same front limbs, not additional arms above four grounded legs. Smooth evenly spaced animation poses with stable volume and clear anticipation, action and recovery.
Transparent background and clear generous transparent gutters; no floor or ground shadow, no labels, text or dialogue box, no collar. Each complete actor, tail and prop comfortably within its own cell. Preserve the reference's coarse geometry and restrained dithered vertex shading. Do not add fluffy fur or smooth modern toy rendering.

Animation: Four-pawed standing fox looks back at one of his three tails, lifts ONE existing foreleg to gently bat its vermilion tip, and puts that SAME paw back down. Only THREE paws remain grounded while the fourth is raised. No additional arm. Return standing neutral.
This is a continuous non-looping motion with gradual acceleration and deceleration. First and last poses must match the supplied connection-pose references when present.
